title_en: MacroVoices #548 Dr. Carly Anderson: Emerging Energy Technologies Roundup
title_zh: MacroVoices #548｜Dr. Carly Anderson（Timescale Ventures）：新兴能源技术全景扫描
subtitle_zh: 核裂变与核聚变复兴、涡轮机与激光浓缩铀、数据中心电力瓶颈的一次全景梳理
description: MacroVoices #548 Dr. Carly Anderson: Emerging Energy Technologies Roundup

turns.en: You can't understate the importance of hyperscalers and data center builders to opening up these new markets and creating the conditions for a nuclear renaissance because you really do need somebody who's willing to sign a 20 year PPA for $100 per megawatt hour.
turns.zh: 你怎么强调超大规模云厂商（hyperscalers）和数据中心建设方在打开这些新市场过程中的重要性都不为过，正是他们为核能复兴（nuclear renaissance）创造了条件，因为你确实需要有人愿意签一份 20 年期、每兆瓦时 100 美元的购电协议（PPA）。

turns.en: And that didn't exist until a couple of years ago. That was Dr. Carly Anderson. I'm Eric Townsend and this is Macrovoices, the free weekly podcast targeting professional finance and sophisticated private investors.
turns.zh: 而在几年前，这样的人根本就不存在。刚才这段话出自 Dr. Carly Anderson。我是 Eric Townsend，这里是 MacroVoices，一档面向专业金融人士和成熟私人投资者的免费周更播客。

turns.en: Episode 548 was produced earlier in August 2026. We've got a special treat lined up for you this Labor Day weekend. Dr. Carly Anderson is one of the smartest and most interesting investors I know.
turns.zh: 第 548 期是在 2026 年 8 月早些时候录制的。这个劳动节（Labor Day）周末，我们给你准备了一份特别的大礼。Dr. Carly Anderson 是我认识的最聪明、最有意思的投资人之一。

turns.en: She's a PhD energy geek whose day job is being a venture capitalist specializing in early stage investments in the energy related technologies that have the potential to change the world.
turns.zh: 她是个有博士学位的能源极客，本职工作是风险投资人，专门投那些有可能改变世界的能源相关技术的早期项目。

turns.en: She's an early investor in aloatomics and a frequent source of new and exciting energy related investment ideas. We'll discuss the formative nuclear renaissance in both nuclear fission and nuclear fusion, turbine technologies, laser enrichment of uranium and much more in this interview.
turns.zh: 她是 Aalo Atomics 的早期投资人，也常常能带来新鲜又刺激的能源类投资点子。在这次访谈里，我们会聊正在成形的核裂变与核聚变这两场核能复兴、涡轮机技术、铀的激光浓缩等等一大堆话题。

turns.en: Joining me now is Dr. Carly Anderson, who is the founder and managing director of timescale.vc. Carly has a PhD in chemical engineering, although it doesn't sound nearly as exciting as what her PhD thesis was on, which was actually creating miniature lightning in order to heal wounds, fascinating stuff.
turns.zh: 现在坐在我身边的是 Dr. Carly Anderson，她是 timescale.vc 的创始人兼董事总经理。Carly 有化学工程博士学位——不过这个头衔听起来远不如她的博士论文有意思，她的论文做的其实是制造微型闪电来愈合伤口，非常有意思的东西。

turns.en: Carly, it's not actually all that surprising that you went from a PhD in plasma to eventually becoming my favorite champion of nuclear fusion energy, but why don't we start with something that we actually agree on, which is nuclear fission.
turns.zh: Carly，你从等离子体（plasma）博士一路走到今天，成了我最喜欢的核聚变能源代言人，这一点其实并不太让人意外。不过我们还是先从一个我们俩真正有共识的话题聊起，那就是核裂变。

turns.en: What do you think are the most exciting things that are going on in terms of this nuclear renaissance? What do investors need to understand about it?
turns.zh: 你觉得眼下这场核能复兴里最让人兴奋的事情是什么？投资人需要理解些什么？

turns.en: Thanks, Eric. It's great to be here. As I think a lot of people have noticed, hopefully it's been a crazy exciting year in terms of ground being broken on new demonstrations for some of the smaller reactors as well as continued progress on the regulatory front and on supply chain maturing for some of the larger designs.
turns.zh: 谢谢你，Eric，很高兴来到这里。我想很多人都已经注意到了，希望这一年确实是极其兴奋的一年：一些较小反应堆的新示范项目开始动工，监管层面也在持续推进，一些较大设计的供应链也在走向成熟。

turns.en: I know you've talked to many people on the show already about the happenings earlier this summer at Idaho National Lab. Fantastic to see so many new companies deploying technology or at least at the first steps for showing that their nuclear cores work.
turns.zh: 我知道你已经在节目上跟很多人聊过今年夏天早些时候在 Idaho National Lab 发生的那些事。看到这么多新公司在部署自己的技术，或者至少迈出了证明自家堆芯能工作的第一步，真是太棒了。

turns.en: In the coming 12 months, I'm sure we'll see many more milestones from some of these smaller reactor companies. Again, I know we're both very excited about this space and being able to come down that cost curve and rapidly iterate on some of these new designs.
turns.zh: 在接下来的 12 个月里，我相信我们会看到这些较小的反应堆公司达成更多里程碑。再说一次，我知道我们俩都对这个领域非常兴奋——兴奋于能把成本曲线压下来、对这些新设计做快速迭代。

turns.en: On the larger end of the spectrum, I think there's a lot of stuff that people don't hear about in the headlines around restarting, obviously, some of the older nuclear plants, potentially one of the fastest ways to get gigawatts of nuclear power back on the grid.
turns.zh: 在更大规模的那一端，我觉得有很多事情是头条新闻里听不到的，比如重启一些老核电站，这大概是最快能让吉瓦级核电重新并网的方式之一。

turns.en: There's also some work going on to increase the power production at existing nuclear plants. And that's an area that I think is super exciting because it's also a way to bring more power online fast, to meet the growing demand that we keep hearing about from the electricity sector, to power data centers and all kinds of new infrastructure in the US.
turns.zh: 另外还有一些工作是在提升现有核电站的发电量。这个方向我觉得超级让人兴奋，因为它同样是快速增加电力上线的办法，可以满足我们从电力行业不断听到的那种增长需求——给数据中心供电、给美国各种新型基础设施供电。

turns.en: Let's talk about what it takes to do that, deliver the goal, which is more power, data centers, blah, blah, blah, so forth. Okay, but conventional nuclear power plants take at least a decade to build and sometimes longer than that to get permitted and sorted out and so forth.
turns.zh: 那我们来聊聊要做到这一点需要什么。目标是交付更多电力、给数据中心供电等等等等，好，可是传统核电站至少要建十年，有时候光是拿到许可、把各种事情理顺就要更久。

turns.en: So what are the bottlenecks? And more importantly, what do you think are the technologies or trends or changes or whatever you want to call it that's going to allow us to not have to take upwards of a decade in order to deliver more energy using nuclear technology?
turns.zh: 那瓶颈到底在哪儿？更重要的是，你觉得是哪些技术、趋势或者变化——随你怎么叫——能让我们不必再花上十年以上的时间，才能用核能技术交付更多能源？

turns.en: Great. Well, one of the key things that I think we're both very excited about is mass producing as many components for these reactors as we can.
turns.zh: 好。我觉得我们俩都非常兴奋的一个关键点，就是尽可能大规模量产这些反应堆的各种部件。

turns.en: This is something that should shrink the lead time for everything from the reactor vessels to the pumps that move the fluid around inside these power plants, to the instruments, to the safety mechanisms, to days, if not weeks, if not months.
turns.zh: 这件事应该能把各个环节的交付周期压缩到几天、几周，最多几个月——从反应堆压力容器，到在电厂内部循环流体的泵，到仪表，到安全机构，都是如此。

turns.en: If you look at the time it takes to build a standard nuclear power plant and the standard is that kind of 1000 megawatt chunk, you have to, by the time you get through site works and then concrete pouring and then shipping these massive, massive metal containers to site, I mean, Vogel was way, way over schedule and over budget.
turns.zh: 如果你看看建一座标准核电站要花的时间，标准就是那种 1000 兆瓦的大块头，从场地施工到浇筑混凝土，再把这些巨大巨大的金属容器运到现场——我是说，Vogtle 项目严重超期、严重超预算。

turns.en: I think the best people in the world are installing these in five years. That's not as fat. That's not where we want to be, right? We're looking at designs on the smaller end where you could deploy in less than two years, ideally on months.
turns.zh: 我觉得世界上最好的团队也要五年才能装好。这还不够快，这不是我们想要的位置，对吧？我们看的是小尺寸那一端的设计，理想情况下几个月、最多不到两年就能部署。

turns.en: A typical data center is one building maybe goes up in nine months at this point and you really want your power generation systems to be able to match that timeline.
turns.zh: 一座典型的数据中心就是一栋楼，现在大概九个月就能盖起来，你真的会希望自己的发电系统能匹配上这个时间表。

turns.en: So mass manufacturing love to see that coming out of companies like Aloe Atomics and some of the other ones on the small end of things. In terms of other bottlenecks, it was great to see part 57 released from the NRC to create a pathway for advanced reactors that looks different from the traditional methods for light water reactors.
turns.zh: 所以大规模制造，我很乐意看到 Aalo Atomics 以及小尺寸那一端的其他一些公司把它做出来。至于其他瓶颈，很高兴看到 NRC 发布了 Part 57，为先进反应堆开辟了一条路径，这条路径跟轻水反应堆（light water reactor）的传统审批方式不一样。

turns.en: Those regulations were set up very specifically for technologies and in a way that just isn't applicable to some of the, some of the newer designs.
turns.zh: 那套法规当初是专门针对特定技术、以特定方式制定的，对一些更新的设计根本不适用。

turns.en: It's exciting to see some of the fuel supply chain mature, which we can talk more about and the power generation side of things and like all the other things besides and outside that what we call the nuclear island, which is like where the magic happens and the fuel produces heat.
turns.zh: 看到燃料供应链走向成熟也很让人兴奋，这块我们可以多聊聊；还有发电那一侧，以及核岛（nuclear island）之外所有其他的东西——核岛就是魔法发生的地方，燃料在那里产生热量。

turns.en: All of these components have to come together and we're seeing that happen a lot faster at that smaller one to 20 megawatt scale. Carly, let's talk about how this nuclear Renaissance market is coming together in terms of where the opportunity is.
turns.zh: 所有这些部件必须凑到一起，而在 1 到 20 兆瓦这个较小的尺度上，我们看到这件事正在快得多地发生。Carly，我们来聊聊这个核能复兴市场是怎么成形的，机会到底在哪里。

turns.en: The way I'm seeing this, what we're seeing in terms of grid connected energy is mostly discussion about more light water reactors, good old fashioned Eisenhower era technology nuclear reactors designed to the 1950s, build more of those things. That's the thing to do.
turns.zh: 我是这么看的：在并网电力这块，我们看到的讨论主要还是关于更多的轻水反应堆——老式的、艾森豪威尔（Eisenhower）时代的技术，1950 年代设计的核反应堆，多建一些这种东西，这才是该做的事。

turns.en: Advanced nuclear, the stuff that I tend to get more excited about costs more, at least in the beginning, it'll cost more and that means somebody who can afford to pay up for it has to be the customer and there's not a whole lot of those.
turns.zh: 先进核能，也就是我通常更容易兴奋起来的那类东西，成本更高，至少一开始会更贵；这就意味着必须有一个付得起高价的客户，而这种客户并不多。

turns.en: It seems like what we're seeing is advanced nuclear is really finding three niche markets, which is the military market where people have a Pentagon size budget for whatever special thing and you know, they can just afford to do whatever they want. You've got out in the middle of nowhere, the market that is for micro reactors that is now dominated by large diesel generator sets that run remote mining villages and so forth.
turns.zh: 看起来我们见到的是，先进核能真正在找到三个利基市场：一是军用市场，那里的人有一个五角大楼（Pentagon）规模的预算去买任何特殊的东西，他们想怎么干就能怎么干；二是偏远地区市场，也就是微型反应堆（micro reactor）的市场，现在这块被大型柴油发电机组主导着，给偏远的矿区、村落之类供电。

turns.en: There's a nuclear angle there. They can afford to, you know, if you're right now, if you're what you're spending money on is every week, you got to deliver another flight goes up to the middle of the Arctic Circle someplace just to deliver the next load of diesel fuel for your generators to run whatever you're running up there. If you can replace that with a nuclear reactor, you don't have to make that weekly fuel flight and
turns.zh: 那里有一个核能的切入点。他们付得起这个钱——你知道，如果你现在每周都得再派一架飞机飞到北极圈某个地方，就为了给你的发电机送下一批柴油燃料，让你在那上头运转的东西能继续转，那如果你能用一座核反应堆把它替代掉，你就不用每周飞这一趟燃料航班了，

turns.en: it's a huge cost savings. There's a market there and then the last one seems to be data centers for AI. Would you agree those are the markets? Do you see any other markets and which of those do you think is going to be most exciting and which technologies do you think are going to drive the most profit?
turns.zh: 那就是一笔巨大的成本节约。那里是有市场的。然后最后一个看起来是给 AI 用的数据中心。你同意这些就是那几个市场吗？你还看到别的市场吗？你觉得哪一个会最让人兴奋？你觉得哪些技术会带来最多的利润？

turns.en: Great, Eric. I think that that's a perfect rundown of three key areas for our early nuclear deployment and I'll touch on the first two very quickly. Defense has been a fantastic enabler for so many technologies coming out of American Labs.
turns.zh: 说得好，Eric。我觉得你把早期核能部署的三个关键领域总结得非常到位。前两个我很快带过一下。国防一直是美国实验室出来的这么多技术的绝佳推动者。

turns.en: I think across our portfolio, they've been an early customer able to help buy down technical risk for things in the autonomous transportation space. I think a drone delivery in terms of new materials, in terms of satellite capabilities, that is a fantastic market. It is limited. turns.zh: 契合偏远社区。所以想想矿业设施，想想 Alaska。同样，在那些地方，这些是非常重要的技术，往往没有替代品。

turns.zh: 巨大的。就这一点我说两句，因为我觉得这件事已经让行业里我们很多人沮丧很久了，就是看着全球核能市场上可供选择的东西。你知道，今天全世界大约有 80 座反应堆在建，我想其中大约 60 座是中国设计。
